headline: The magnetic sub-test was non-diagnostic for both models, and we say so for both. Our pre-registered peak metric gives the same -13 to -19 nT magnitudes on ordinary non-eclipse days, so neither the dome's range nor ours is confirmed by it. On the dome's own named instrument (the Z component), the deepest excursion at any priority station is -4.1 nT and the largest eclipse-shaped fit is -7.6 nT, well short of the dome's -17 to -21 nT, even though a signal that size would have been visible through that day's noise; and the dome's signature timing (peaks at first and last contact) is absent at every priority station, where a dome-sized signal would have stood out 6-25 times above the noise. The small eclipse-shaped features we could find, including a few nT at the Iberian stations, also show up at observatories the eclipse never reached (Hermanus, Ascension), so we do not claim them as eclipse signals either. The geometric sub-test (294 km path vs the dome's 1.3 km) remains the decisive result - and one of our own geometric numbers (Hartland 88%) missed its registered bound; the true value was about 94%.

symmetric_evaluation_rules.SR-1_kp_gate: One rule for both sides. Every pre-registered criterion that carries a Kp<2 precondition - ours (B1-M-001, OBS-D-02, OBS-D-04, OBS-S-02) and the dome's (PRED-095 'IF Kp<2', Tier-1 'falsification only on verified Kp<2 day', Tier-3 'Kp<2 entire Aug 9-12', live countdown 'Requires Kp < 2') - is formally UNTESTED: GFZ definitive Kp was 2.333 for 18-21 UT on 2026-08-12 and 3.0 for 15-18 UT on 2026-08-11. Note the dome text also leaves Kp 2-3 unspecified: 'IF Kp >= 3, signal will be buried in storm noise (not a falsification)' (monitor/baseline/03-predictions.txt:74) while validity requires Kp<2 (:91); 2.333 falls in the gap.
symmetric_evaluation_rules.DR-1_detectability_override: Beyond the formal status, a prediction is scored 'as-if' ONLY for the part of its predicted amplitude that exceeds 3 x the empirical null SD of the same metric on the same UT window, estimated from the preceding 30 days with Kp(12-24 UT) <= 3 (i.e. at noise levels comparable to or worse than the eclipse day). The same rule is applied to our ranges and to the dome's. Below that threshold a claim is 'untested at this noise level', not confirmed and not refuted. Detection power for a -17 nT signal was checked by injection into real control-day noise (per-station table in z_component_evaluation).
symmetric_evaluation_rules.DQ-1_publication_state: A station is excluded from every absolute-baseline (protocol-metric) criterion if the 16-20 UT median H of its quiet-day set spans more than 50 nT (about 3x the largest span, 16 nT, at any station). Only GUI trips it (~185 nT step between July quasi-definitive and August variation files). Applied uniformly to OBS-D-02 counts, PRED-095 tallies, B1-M-001, B2-M-001/002 and OBS-O-01. Offset-immune template fits are unaffected and are still reported for GUI.
symmetric_evaluation_rules.CTL-1_control_stations: Any candidate eclipse feature is checked against non-eclipsed observatories with the SAME template and window: ASC (Ascension, zero obscuration, Sun 13 to -1 deg over 18-19 UT, dayside), KOU (Kourou, zero obscuration, full daylight), HER (Hermanus, zero obscuration, NIGHT side after ~16:15 UT - correcting the cycle-1 review, which described HER as dayside). A feature that a non-eclipsed control reproduces at similar z is not attributed to the eclipse.

conditions.preregistered_kp_lt_2_met: PARTIAL — met 16:00-18:00 UT, NOT met 18:00-21:00 UT (Kp 2+). Every station's +/-60 min evaluation window (max-coverage times 17:58-18:54 UT) straddles the 18:00 boundary. Strictly, the Kp<2 precondition of B1-M-001, OBS-D-02, OBS-D-04 and OBS-S-02 is NOT satisfied for any station.
conditions.geomagnetic_context: Storm on 2026-08-08 (Kp 6-, Dst min -59 nT); 2026-08-12 is recovery-phase. Kyoto realtime (quick-look) Dst, eclipse-day minus quiet-day-set mean: -12.0 (16-17UT), -11.6 (17-18UT), -13.8 (18-19UT), -15.0 (19-20UT) nT. Source https://wdc.kugi.kyoto-u.ac.jp/dst_realtime/202608/index.html (quick-look, subject to revision).
conditions.geomagnetic_context_revised: Recovery phase of the 2026-08-08 storm. Kyoto quick-look Dst on the eclipse day sits about 12-15 nT below the quiet-day-set mean over 16-20 UT (quick-look, subject to revision). Station H responds to a ring-current change roughly as Dst x cos(magnetic latitude); with a centred dipole (pole ~80.8N, 72.6W) the factors are ~0.73-0.77 in Iberia (EBR, SPT, SFS), ~0.59-0.65 at HAD/NGK/CLF and ~0.47-0.54 at ESK/LER, i.e. about -6 to -10 nT of H for a -13 nT Dst offset. That is a plausible CONTRIBUTOR to the -8 to -11 nT window-mean depressions, not the whole story: LER's 14-16 UT mean was only -4.1 nT against a window mean of -11.2, and the quietest control day (2026-08-06, Kp 0.333) produced protocol-metric values of -6 to -18 nT with no storm at all.

methods.data: INTERMAGNET 1-minute data via BGS GIN web service (https://imag-data.bgs.ac.uk/GIN_V1/GINServices, publicationState=best-avail, per-day requests), 2026-07-13..2026-08-12. H = recorded H, or sqrt(X^2+Y^2) for XYZ-reporting observatories. Fetched 2026-09-26.
methods.obscuration: Computed, not taken from the NASA web calculator: skyfield 1.55 + JPL DE421 topocentric apparent Sun/Moon, WGS84 station coordinates from IAGA-2002 headers, area-overlap of the solar disc at 1-min cadence 15:00-21:00 UT. Validation: greatest eclipse reproduced at 17:45 UT at 65.225N/25.228W with obscuration 1.0 (NASA 17:45:53.8); 2017-08-21 Boulder max at 17:46 UT, 93.6% (matches published local circumstances within ~1 pp). Deviation from the protocol (which named the NASA local-circumstances calculator) is disclosed; an independent NASA-calculator cross-check is recommended before publication.
methods.quiet_days: Protocol step 2 read as: days with max 3-h Kp <= 1 in the 30 days preceding the event, ties/fill by lowest daily Kp sum. Only 4 days satisfy max Kp<=1 (07-19, 07-20, 08-01, 08-06); 5th filled with 08-05 (sum 3.33). Sensitivity set ranked purely by daily sum: 08-06, 08-05, 08-07, 07-19, 08-01. Baseline = per-UT-minute mean over quiet days (finer than the protocol's "same UT-hour"; the difference is sub-nT for this window).
methods.protocol_metric: Peak = max |signed deviation| in +/-60 min around each station's computed max-coverage minute (exact protocol step 2).
methods.supplementary_metric_NOT_PREREGISTERED: Eclipse-isolating detrend: fit a line to the deviation over [first contact-60 min, first contact] and [last contact, last contact+60 min], subtract, report mean residual over [t_max-30, t_max+30]. Empirical null = the same statistic on the same UT windows on every non-quiet day of the preceding 30 days with Kp(15-21UT) <= 2.67 (n=13-19 per station). Sensitivity: anchor 30 vs 60 min, linear vs quadratic.
methods.components: H (our frozen protocol's component) AND Z (the dome's named Tier-1 instrument, monitor/baseline/03-predictions.txt:107). Both use the same quiet-day per-minute baseline. X/Y/F are available in the scripts but not scored (the dome's pattern clause is moot once amplitude fails).
methods.quiet_days_interpretation: 'Kp <= 1' in protocol step 2 is read as max 3-h GFZ Kp <= 1.0; 1+ (1.333) does NOT qualify. Four days satisfy it (07-19, 07-20, 08-01, 08-06); 08-05 (max Kp 1.333 in 12-24 UT but lowest daily sum 3.33 among the rest) fills the fifth slot per the tie/fill rule. EBR, CLF, BEL and SFS use 4 days because their 2026-08-01 files contain no valid samples 15-21 UT (data gaps); no day was dropped for publication state.
methods.leave_one_out: For control-day statistics the day being evaluated is removed from its own baseline (leave-one-out) so quiet days are not compared with themselves.
methods.joint_template_fit_NOT_PREREGISTERED: Replaces the cycle-1 window-mean detrend as the primary eclipse-isolating metric (the window-mean compared a mean to peak predictions and attenuated lagged signals). Model over [local C1-60, local C4+60]: dev(t) = a + b t + A s(t), with s(t) a template normalised to peak 1, so A is directly a PEAK-equivalent amplitude in nT with the trend fitted simultaneously. Templates: obscuration(t) passed through a first-order recovery lag tau = 0, 15, 30, 60 min; local C1/C4 contact-phase (Gaussians, sigma 10 min, at each station's own first and last contact); global C1/C4 contact-phase (16:59 and 21:01 UT, the contact times in the dome's own post_eclipse_analysis() code, monitor/baseline/03-predictions.txt:191-195), window 15:59-22:01. Injection into real control-day noise recovers A at 100% for all tau (linear model).
methods.window_mean_detrend_retained_as_sensitiv: The cycle-1 metric is kept only as a sensitivity check. Injection-recovery of its window mean (signal peak-normalised): 100% at tau 0, 95% at 15 min, 83% at 30 min, 61% at 60 min; window-mean/peak ratio ~0.65-0.72. The pre-contact-only extrapolation variant has null SD 6-15 nT and is non-informative (table in per_station).
methods.correlation_tests: Pearson r between the linearly-detrended deviation and each template over the same windows, reproducing the dome's r > 0.7 (success) / r > 0.5 (falsification) thresholds, with the same statistic computed on every control day for a false-positive rate.

Same protocol metric (max |signed dev| within +/-60 min of each station's t_max, leave-one-out quiet baseline) applied to all 30 preceding days. Evaluable dome stations: EBR, SPT, ESK, LER, HAD, NGK, CLF (GUI excluded under DQ-1; COI no data).

z_component_evaluation.why: Curmudgeon critical hole: the dome's Tier-1 claim names the INTERMAGNET 1-min Z component, pattern Z down, correlated with 'umbra contact geometry', and separately claims peaks at C1 and C4, not at maximum (monitor/baseline/03-predictions.txt:104-109). Its 2026-03-15 revision instead says 'Z minimum within 30 minutes of maximum eclipse coverage' (:72-73), and its own analysis code correlates against GLOBAL contact times 16:59 / 21:01 UT (:191-195). We evaluate all three readings on Z so the result does not depend on picking one.

reading_R1_Z_minimum_within_30min_of_max.result: Z minima in the +/-60 min window: EBR -4.12, SPT -0.27, HAD -2.18, CLF -1.59, NGK -0.33, ESK -2.86 nT (priority stations); LER -3.42. The minimum does fall within 30 min of max coverage at most stations, but a timing hit on its own is weak (about half of any +/-60 min window lies within +/-30 min) and the depth is 13-21 nT short of -17..-21 at every priority station.

reading_R2_local_contact_phase.result: r(detrended Z, local C1/C4 template) = EBR +0.20, SPT +0.28, HAD +0.14, CLF +0.07, NGK -0.27, ESK -0.16. None reaches the dome's 0.5 'coherent signal' level, let alone 0.7. Joint-fit contact-phase amplitude on Z: EBR -1.7 nT (3-sigma detectable 4.3 nT), SPT -1.6 nT (3-sigma detectable 2.0 nT), HAD -1.2 nT (3-sigma detectable 2.8 nT), CLF -0.2 nT (3-sigma detectable 2.5 nT), NGK +1.4 nT (3-sigma detectable 3.7 nT), ESK +1.3 nT (3-sigma detectable 4.0 nT). A -17 nT contact-phase signal would have been 12-25 sigma and detected on 100% of injected control days; it is absent.

reading_R3_global_contacts_1659_2101.result: r(detrended Z, global template) = EBR +0.20, SPT -0.17, HAD -0.19, CLF -0.22, NGK -0.22, ESK -0.01; joint-fit amplitudes EBR -1.9, SPT +1.2, HAD +1.6, CLF +0.8, NGK +1.3, ESK +0.1 nT. Absent on Z. (H shows 2-6 nT drops at both 16:59 and 21:01 at NGK, WNG, BEL, LER - see dome_favourable_findings; on 2026-08-12 itself, 13% of arbitrary time pairs 4 h 02 min apart show the same double drop at 3+ of those 4 stations, 4.7% on an average control day.)

obscuration_shaped_fit.result: Z joint-fit amplitudes with an obscuration template (tau 0) are negative at every priority station: EBR -6.1 (z -1.4), SPT -4.0 (z -1.3), HAD -5.5 (z -1.7), CLF -2.8 (z -0.8), NGK -3.6 (z -1.2), ESK -7.6 (z -2.4) nT - the dome's 'Z down' sign, at roughly a quarter to a third of its amplitude. BUT the non-eclipsed dayside control ASC gives -2.5 (z -2.1), -2.0 (z -1.8), -5.0 (z -3.1), -4.3 (z -2.9), -5.3 (z -3.2), -5.9 (z -3.2) nT with the same templates, so the negative-Z shape is common to stations the eclipse never touched and is not attributed to the eclipse (CTL-1).

z_component_evaluation.detectability_summary: Injected -17 nT (peak) obscuration-shaped signal is recovered at >= 3 sigma on 84-100% of control days at all six priority stations on Z; the contact-phase templates on 100%. The dome's amplitude was testable at this noise level under DR-1; the lower half of our own B1-M-001 range (-5 to about -10 nT) was not (3-sigma thresholds 7-15 nT on Z, 8-22 nT on H depending on station and tau).

control_station_check.lagged_H_fit_reproduced_at_HER: The strongest eclipse-shaped H result anywhere - lagged-obscuration fits at the southern stations (tau 30: EBR -8.5 (z -2.9), SPT -8.8 (z -3.4), SFS -12.2 (z -3.0) nT) - is reproduced at Hermanus with the SAME templates (tau 30: -8.8 (z -3.1), -9.5 (z -3.4), -10.2 (z -3.6)). Hermanus had no eclipse and was in darkness. The feature is a slow late-window decline common to both hemispheres, which a lagged template absorbs. Not attributed to the eclipse.
control_station_check.18_4x_feature: Relative to 16:00-16:30 UT: HER -1.2 (18:38) to -3.5 nT (18:53); KOU +7.2 (18:38) falling to +5.4 (18:47); NGK/WNG/BEL show a positive pulse at 18:38 then a 3-5 nT fall to 18:47, the same shape as KOU. The 18:46-18:48 protocol peaks are part of a feature recorded at non-eclipsed stations on both day and night sides.
control_station_check.pre_C1_step: At 16:57-17:00 UT H drops 3-5 nT at NGK, WNG, BEL, LER and ESK (10-min step: NGK -3.1, WNG -4.0, BEL -3.0, LER -6.0, ESK -5.4 nT) and ~1 nT at HER. Local first contact at NGK/WNG/BEL was 17:14-17:17, so this is 15+ minutes BEFORE the penumbra reached them - it cannot be caused by the eclipse under either model. The 17:09 'protocol peaks' at NGK, WNG and BEL are the first minute of their +/-60 min windows (window starts 17:07-17:09): the depression was largest before the window opened and eased as the eclipse began.

OBS_D_02.as_if: Fires at 6 of 7 evaluable stations, but fires on 24 of 30 control days (SC-5). Fired, NON-DIAGNOSTIC; no evidential weight.

OBS_D_03.note: Dome coverage and computed obscuration are rank-correlated at r12=0.978 across the 7 stations, so the paired test has essentially no power at n=7. The "Borrowed" trilemma branch is not empirically separable with this station set.

OBS_D_04.as_if: Does not fire: no station shows an eclipse-attributable signed amplitude in [-25,-5] nT that survives CTL-1 (the southern-station lagged fits are reproduced at Hermanus).

OBS_S_02.as_if: Does not fire, and could not have fired: the |peak| < 1 nT condition is below our own pre-committed 2 nT noise floor and is met at 0 stations on all 31 days examined (SC-5).

criteria.OBS_S_03: NOT EVALUATED - no independent observed per-station obscuration; computed values are themselves standard-physics predictions.

OBS_O_01.detail: GUI's protocol value (-92.39 nT) meets the letter of OBS-O-01 (< -50 nT). GUI is excluded from every absolute-baseline criterion by the pre-stated DQ-1 rule (185 nT publication-state level step in its baseline), not by judgment; its same-state baseline gives -19.6 nT. No other station is positive-signed or below -50 nT.

OBS_O_02.detail: The magnetic bucket was not a clean test of either model. Unanticipated conditions: storm-recovery variability (Kp 2.333 in the evaluation window), a quiet-day baseline that non-eclipse days also depart from by 6-18 nT, and external features at 16:57-17:00 and 18:38-18:53 UT recorded at non-eclipsed control stations. Our pre-registered criteria were also miscalibrated (SC-5). Per OBS-O-02 we publicly note the limit: 2026-08-12 did not provide the clean magnetic test we registered.

OBS_O_03.detail: Dome centrals (B2-M-001) matched within 2 nT at only 1 of 7 stations; candidate stations show raw deviations comparable to dome stations.

B1-G-005.detail: Registered 88% +/- 2 pp. Hartland (51.00N, 4.48W): DE421/skyfield 94.36% obscuration, max 18:15 UT, partial 17:18-19:08 UT (1 h 50 min). Independent ephemeris: timeanddate.com local circumstances for Bideford (51.017N, 4.205W, ~20 km E), fetched 2026-09-27: began 17:17, maximum 18:14 at magnitude 0.947, ended 19:08 UT, duration 1 h 51 min (DE421 at the Bideford coordinates: 94.16% obscuration, same times). Our registered value was ~6 pp low, ~4 pp beyond its own bound. The review's 'roughly 2 h 45 min' partial duration (data/sections.json part4 section 4.2.7) is ~55 min too long. Correction text for 4.2.7 and the other surfaces was supplied in EXP-684 (WIN-010.c16 hole 4 / ISS-3082); it can land as a dated erratum independently of this magnetic revision. The headline geometric result (294 km vs 1.317 km) is unaffected.

B1-M-001.as_if: NOT CONFIRMED. The protocol metric lands in [-25,-5] at 12 of 12 high-obscuration stations, but does so at >= half the stations on 17 of 30 control days - non-diagnostic (SC-5). Under DR-1 the upper part of our range (about -25 to -12 nT eclipse-attributable) was testable and is not observed at any station after CTL-1; the lower part (-5 to about -10 nT) was below the 3-sigma detectability threshold at most stations and is untested. See SC-1.

registered_prediction_scorecard.B2-G-001..004: Scored in the geometric bucket (2026-08-13) - unchanged.

B2-M-001.detail: Protocol metric within +/-2 nT of the frozen dome central at 1 of 7 stations (HAD); obscuration-template tau 0 fit: 0 of 7; lagged fits bring EBR and SPT within ~2 nT of -10.66/-9.82 but Hermanus reproduces those fits (CTL-1). The global-contact H fit at NGK (-7.8 nT) is within 2 nT of the NGK central (-6.67) - reported in dome_favourable_findings; 1 of 7.

B2-M-002.detail: Registered: 8 of 9 dome stations |dB| < 2 nT. Protocol metric: 0 of 7. Cycle-1 window-mean detrend: 4 of 7 (CLF -0.29, HAD +1.62, NGK +1.60, ESK +1.57). Tau-0 joint fit: 1 of 7 (CLF +0.3). Not met at 8 of 9 under any metric. Even if it had been, near-zero eclipse-attributable values are also what a sunset-eclipse Chapman-Sq response buried in noise looks like (SC-1), and B2-M-002 is our derivation of what dome geometry forces, which contradicts the dome's own formula (the trilemma) - so this prediction could not discriminate on this day.

PRED_095.claim: -17 to -21 nT at >80% coverage stations ('IF Kp < 2 ... Z minimum within 30 minutes of maximum eclipse coverage', monitor/baseline/03-predictions.txt:71-75)
PRED_095.formal: UNTESTED by the dome's own precondition (SR-1).
PRED_095.as_if_DR1: Dome's >80%-coverage stations (its own table: EBR 95%, SPT 90%; COI no data): Z minima -4.1 and -0.3 nT; Z obscuration-fit amplitudes -6.1 and -4.0 nT with 3-sigma detectability 10.5 and 8.1 nT; H eclipse-attributable fits -2.9 and -4.1 nT (tau 0). A -17 nT signal was detectable at both on 89-100% of injected control days and is not present on either component. Raw H protocol values (-13.7, -15.6) are not in range and are matched by ordinary days anyway.
PRED_095.recommended_verdict: falsified (as-if under DR-1, with the precondition override stated in the note) - PRIMARY; alternative for operator: standard_physics (dome labels Tier 1 'Globe-Compatible' and PRED-095 restates WIN-068). Use the same label strength as PRED-TIER-1; do not split them.
PRED_095.proposed_note: [2026-09-xx post-event magnetic results, pending OTS] The dome's own Kp<2 precondition was not met (GFZ Kp 2.333 for 18-21 UT), so by its own terms the test is void, and we say so first. We evaluated it anyway under one rule applied to both sides: a predicted amplitude is scored only if it is at least 3x the measured noise on comparable days. -17 to -21 nT clears that bar easily; it is not present at Ebro or San Pablo on the dome's Z component (deepest excursions -4.1 and -0.3 nT) or on H. Our own -5 to -25 nT range gets the same treatment and is not confirmed either. Results: predictions/eclipse-2026-08-12-results.json.

dome_live_scoring_entry.kappa_double_application: The live formula is not a second, independent baseline. 10.9 x 1.672 = 18.22 (the frozen BOU baseline times kappa), and the -28.9 nT EBR/SPT prediction = 18.22 x 0.95 x 1.672: kappa is used again in place of the Ebro FSF, which the dome's own table gives as 1.029 (monitor/baseline/03-predictions.txt:115; that would give -17.8 nT). Kappa is applied twice. This corroborates WIN-010.c16 hole 6 and should replace the 'two baselines' wording in ISS-3090 / EXP-685.
dome_live_scoring_entry.assessment: Against the dome's own live rule ('fails if within +/-3 nT of 0'): eclipse-attributable H at EBR is -2.9 nT (tau 0 fit) and SPT -4.1; on Z -6.1 and -4.0. Raw H (-13.7, -15.6) passes a one-sided zero test but ordinary days pass it too, and it misses -28.9 by 13-15 nT. The rule is ill-posed: it scores a raw deviation against zero with no baseline for non-eclipse variability, and its 'globe_prediction: 0.0' misstates standard physics, which predicts a non-zero, conductivity-scaled Chapman-Sq effect.

dome_favourable_findings: Raw H at every dome-cited station sat 13-19 nT below the quiet-day baseline during the eclipse window. Real, reproduced - and matched by ordinary days (2026-08-06, Kp 0.333: -6 to -18 nT).

At both of the dome's global contact times (16:59 and 21:01 UT) H dropped 2-6 nT at NGK, WNG, BEL and LER. On that day's activity level this double coincidence occurs for ~13% of arbitrary time pairs (4.7% on an average control day); it is absent on Z; amplitudes are a quarter or less of the dome's; the r > 0.7 template test does not fire.
NGK's global-contact H fit (-7.8 nT, z -2.5) is within 2 nT of the dome's frozen NGK central (-6.67). One station of seven.
Z-down obscuration-shaped fits at all six priority stations (-2.8 to -7.6 nT). The sign matches the dome's pattern clause; the non-eclipsed ASC shows the same shape (-2.0 to -5.9 nT).
Lagged H fits at EBR and SPT (-8.5 / -8.8 nT at tau 30) sit near the dome's frozen EBR/SPT centrals (-10.66 / -9.82). Hermanus, with no eclipse, gives -8.8 / -9.5 with the same templates.

self_corrections.finding: Our range was drawn from daytime-eclipse ensembles and not scaled for a near-sunset eclipse (Sun 5-14 deg at maximum). The data cannot confirm it: the protocol metric 'hits' it on ordinary days, the eclipse-attributable fits that reach the -5..-12 nT part of the range are reproduced at a non-eclipsed control, and the lower part of the range is below that day's detectability. The observed residuals are compatible with the low end of our range under a lagged-recovery model and with zero. The cycle-1 statement that no station showed a >= 5 nT dip came partly from comparing a window mean with a peak range, and is withdrawn.

Standard Sq physics gives a latitude-dependent sign relative to the Sq current focus; a uniform negative sign for all European stations was over-specified. Descriptively, cycle-1 detrended residuals were negative south of about 45N (EBR, SPT, SFS, GUI, SUA) and weakly positive north of about 49N (ESK, HAD, NGK, MAB, DOU, WNG, BEL), with LER and CLF as exceptions. The boundary was noticed after the fact and the stations share a common external field, so this is reported descriptively, not as evidence.

honest_limits: Kp<2 precondition unmet for 18-21 UT on 2026-08-12 (and for Aug 9-12 per the dome's Tier-3 clause); every magnetic result is formally untested and reported as-if under SR-1/DR-1.

DR-1, DQ-1, CTL-1, the joint template fit and the control-station set were defined after the event, in response to the cycle-1 review. They are applied identically to both sides, but they are not pre-registered.
Obscuration is computed with DE421/skyfield rather than the NASA web calculator named in the protocol; Hartland is cross-checked against timeanddate.com.
Three control stations (ASC, KOU, HER) only; HER is night-side. A fuller non-eclipsed control set would sharpen CTL-1.
Dst values are Kyoto quick-look; ring-current scaling uses a centred dipole.

kernel_of_truth: Two real things sit under the dome's eclipse claims. First, eclipses really do disturb ground magnetometers, and on 2026-08-12 the raw readings at the dome's stations really were 13-19 nT low - a defender looking only at those numbers would see a hit. Second, the dome's insistence on a quiet-day (Kp<2) precondition is good practice, and this day failed it. Both are true. Neither saves the claim: ordinary days produce the same raw numbers, the dome's own named component shows nothing near its amplitude, its signature contact-phase timing is absent where it would have stood out clearly, and the only eclipse-shaped features we could find also appear at observatories the eclipse never reached. A void test is not a confirmation, and 47 days later the dome's own live scoreboard still reads PENDING.
